Introduction
This document provides essential information on the components of the Controversial Sourcing Key
Issue to enable users of ESG Ratings to understand how MSCI Sustainability & Climate’s (MSCI S&C’s)
outputs are determined. Controversial Sourcing is a Key Issue in the Social Pillar of the MSCI ESG
Ratings model. Companies are evaluated on their dependence on, and purchasing volume of, raw
materials procured from conflict areas and their efforts at traceability and certification.
For additional details on the MSCI ESG Ratings Model, refer to the Data, ratings and scores section of
“ESG Ratings Methodology.”

Risks associated with this Key Issue
• Reputational risk and potential loss of market share as consumer awareness grows.
• Costs to comply with new regulations (e.g., Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive
(CSDDD), U.S. Dodd-Frank Act).

Controversial Sourcing Practices score
The Controversial Sourcing Practices score evaluates the company’s ability to manage its exposure to
risks related to its dependence on, and purchasing volume of, raw materials procured from conflict areas
and its efforts at traceability and certification. This score is equal to the Controversial Sourcing
Management score (excluding controversies) and considers attributes of the company's policies and
initiatives. It is expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong initiatives.
• Extent of efforts to ensure compliance with controversial materials sourcing policy
Definition: Indicates whether the company carries out initiatives to ensure compliance with its
controversial sourcing policy, or collaborates with stakeholders to promote supply chain transparency
and accountability.
• Targets for ensuring compliance with controversial materials sourcing policy
Definition: Indicates whether the company has targets for ensuring compliance with its controversial
materials sourcing policy.

• Extent of supplier/material certification as conflict-free by external agencies using the most
stringent criteria
Definition: The extent of relevant products externally certified as conflict-free using the most stringent
criteria, which may differ from industry to industry. Example: Responsible Minerals Assurance Process
(RMAP) for Consumer Electronics.
• Commitments to address controversial sourcing practices
Definition: Indicates whether the company has a policy to address sourcing and use of raw materials
that may originate from areas associated with human rights violations, illicit trade and/or financing of
violence.
• Extent of material traceability to place of origin
Definition: Indicates the estimated share of relevant products with traceable origin of raw materials.
Traceable origin refers to the location where the ore was mined, to the best detail possible. At a
minimum, the description must include the country, but more details may be provided including the
province/state, city, mine site and mine name.

based on the severity, status, and the company’s role in the controversy. The following categories of

Business Segment Exposure score
The Business Segment Exposure score of a business segment is based on a mapping of the business
segment as disclosed by the company to a corresponding business activity. MSCI S&C uses the
Standard Industrial Classification (SIC) system along with industry-specific adjustments to define
business activities. The score associated with a business activity is used to calculate a Business
Segment Exposure score.
The Business Segment Exposure score represents the degree to which a business activity depends on
conflict minerals tin, tantalum, tungsten, and gold as defined under the U.S. Dodd-Frank Act. The score
ranges from 0 to 10, with higher values indicating greater dependency. The metric is derived by applying
Large Language Model (LLM) analysis to Form SD filings submitted by companies to the Securities and
Exchange Commission. These filings contain disclosures on conflict minerals due diligence and usage.
The LLM text analysis extracts conflict minerals usage patterns, which is categorized by the extent of
conflict mineral use. The Dependency score for each business activity is calculated based on the
aggregated usage patterns of companies with relevant operations, providing a standardized measure of
conflict minerals dependency at the activity level.
